cases.expectedBehaviour: The whole normalized prompt equals a declared phrase, so both lexical arms return its owning document at the exact class.
Both arms lowercase before matching, so an all-caps prompt resolves identically to the exact-phrase case.
Every run of non-alphanumeric characters collapses to one separator, so hyphens and slashes resolve to the same normalized phrase.

A three-character token is admitted mid-token by the substring gate, so both arms return the documents whose phrases merely contain it. The scope keeps the case bounded so the admission itself is what is measured.
A contiguous subset of a longer declared phrase scores as phrase containment in both arms.

cases.expectedBehaviour: No token appears anywhere in the corpus, so both arms return an empty result rather than a degraded guess.
The same phrase is declared in several packets. Scoping to one packet must return only that packet's documents in both arms, with no leakage from the others.
The legacy arm returns an archived document at the exact class and the index returns nothing, because the archived tree is outside the index corpus.

The lane filters on an expiry column the index does not model at all. The owning row has no expiry, so both arms return it; the baseline records how many rows in the snapshot are actually expired, since a filter that matches nothing proves nothing on its own.
A document whose leading block is not YAML frontmatter contributes no phrases, so neither lexical arm returns it while ripgrep still finds the text in its body.
One phrase declared by four documents returns all four in both arms; the mapping is many-to-many and no owner is collapsed away.
